Subject: Re: Fwd: [Escalation] Sudden p99 spike and increased 500s on production - RetailFlow

Quick findings from runtime logs (14:35-15:10 UTC):
- At 14:47:32 UTC we applied a TTL smoothing rollout (service: cache-coordinator) intended to reduce stale prefixes. One of the rollout shards incorrectly interpreted the config delta and triggered an aggressive flush for ~0.8% of hot prefixes.
- cache_miss_rate for the affected shard jumped from 0.6% -> 23.7% between 14:48-14:56 UTC.
- We also saw increased cold-model instantiations and backend calls to storage for KV fetches, which matches the higher p99.
- No model changes or infra scaling events at the same time; this looks like a cache invalidation storm.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Roll back the TTL smoothing rollout (already queued, awaiting ops approval).
2) Trigger targeted prefix repopulation for the affected RetailFlow prefixes (low-risk, will warm KV cache entries).
3) Temporarily enable a grace headroom policy that routes RetailFlow traffic to a warmed pool (if available) to shave p95/p99.

I'll start the rollback now and report back in ~10 minutes with metrics.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attached snippets: cache_eviction_trace.log (excerpted), metrics spike chart (inline)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Nina Park <nina.park@retailflow.com>
Cc: ops+oncall@retailflow.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Escalation] Sudden p99 spike and increased 500s on production - RetailFlow

Nina — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We have identified a likely cause: an aggressive TTL smoothing rollout triggered a targeted invalidation of a small set of hot prefixes, which cascaded into a cache-miss storm and backend cold-paths.

Actions we've taken (15:28 UTC onward):
- Paused and rolled back the TTL smoothing rollout that caused the invalidations.
- Initiated targeted repopulation for your top prefixes and increased the KV warmup aggressiveness for your keys.
- Enabled a temporary routing headroom to warmed capacity so your traffic avoids cold-model instantiations where possible.

Early telemetry indicates p95 is trending back towards baseline; p99 should improve as prefixes warm over the next ~10-25 minutes. We're watching the telemetry and will update every 10 minutes until stable.

Would you like a quick 15-minute bridge to walk through the actions and share logs? We can make ourselves available immediately.

Apologies for the impact — we'll follow up with a full postmortem and remediation plan (including safer TTL rollout gates).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
